model_numbers: XT2605-series (Models line not published on GSMArena)
price_brl: R$3.499 suggested at launch (Mar 2026, motorola.com.br); street ~R$2.969 open-sale by Jun 2026 (mobilemasr) — sources disagree on launch band
notes: Upgraded Fusion variant (50 MP AF ultrawide vs the Fusion's 13 MP; adds 10 MP 3x tele). Launched in Brazil Mar 2026 as part of the three-model Edge 70 wave; NOT in Motorola India's lineup as of Jun 2026 (India sells Edge 70 Fusion + Edge 70 Pro+ instead). GSMArena confirms 50 MP f/2.2 120-deg ultrawide with AF, Snapdragon 7s Gen 4, Android 16.
caveats: 120-deg UW comfortably clears the >=118 bar on paper, but Motorola's third-party Camera2 ultrawide exposure is historically mixed (GameChanger: UW IDs hidden on older models; newer Edge models report success) — runtime probe required; whether the UW is reachable via CONTROL_ZOOM_RATIO <1.0 vs a separate ID is undocumented. Snapdragon 7s Gen 4 = known-good Qualcomm Venus encoder family (CBR honored, no B-frame insertion reports). Too new to appear on the ARCore certified list (list lag) — Edge family historically certified, so IMU/timestamp rated likely, not pass. Thermal: efficient 4 nm part, large battery, no sustained-capture data yet. Brazil-only — exclude from India-facing list.

notes: Announced Apr 22, 2026; released Apr 29, 2026. GSMArena confirms 50 MP f/2.0 122-deg ultrawide with PDAF and Dimensity 8500 Extreme, Android 16 + 3 OS upgrades. Sold in both India (Reliance Digital/Flipkart coverage) and Brazil (Tecnoblog). Periscope tele availability is market/region dependent (irrelevant to gates).
caveats: 122-deg UW with PDAF clears the FOV bar comfortably, but Motorola third-party Camera2 UW exposure must be probed per model (historically hidden; newer Edge models OK). Encoder is the main risk: Dimensity 8500 Extreme is a new upper-mid MediaTek — the MTK encoder family ignores frame timestamps (WebRTC forces FRAMERATE_ADJUSTMENT) and CBR compliance is mixed even on Dimensity 8000/9000; verify isBitrateModeSupported(CBR) + track-header 1080p at compat-check. Not yet on the ARCore list (lag); Edge family historically certified. Thermal on a 4 nm upper-mid SoC plausible but unmeasured.

price_inr: Rs 47,999 (12/256, launch Jun 11, 2026; effective Rs 44,999 with offers)
notes: Announced Jun 1, 2026; India sale Jun 11, 2026 via Flipkart + motorola.in. Adds 50MP 3.5x periscope tele over the Pro. FOV CONFIRMED at 122 deg with autofocus by GSMArena + fonearena + beebom launch coverage — the 112 deg figure in some Indian coverage is a typo of the same module. Not in Motorola Brazil's lineup as of Jun 2026 (BR sells Edge 70 Pro instead).
caveats: Same camera+SoC platform as Edge 70 Pro: 122-deg UW confirmed (ignore the 112-deg typo in some Indian coverage), but Motorola third-party Camera2 UW exposure needs a runtime probe, and the Dimensity 8500 Extreme encoder inherits MediaTek's mixed CBR/timestamp record — gate on isBitrateModeSupported(CBR) at compat-check. Not yet ARCore-listed (lag); Edge family historically certified. India-only — exclude from Brazil-facing list.

notes: Brazil-first launch (Mar 2020, ~R$1.299). Never sold in India (India got G8 Power Lite, which has no ultrawide). Long discontinued. ARCore certified ('moto g8' on the certified-device list).
caveats: 118-deg UW passes on paper, but this is exactly the Motorola era where UW camera IDs were hidden from third-party apps (GameChanger evidence), and CONTROL_ZOOM_RATIO only exists after the Android 11 update — logical-multi-camera zoom-out on a 2020 budget HAL is doubtful; expect compat-check rejection on the UW gate. Snapdragon 665 is in the reliable Qualcomm encoder family but is an 11 nm 2019 budget part — 25-min sustained 1080p30 thermal unproven. ARCore certified, so IMU rate + REALTIME timestamps are likely. Discontinued, Android 11 max (no further updates).

notes: Quad camera incl. 8 MP ultrawide + 8 MP tele. Sold officially in Brazil; India launch was never confirmed (Indian sites only listed import pricing). Discontinued. ARCore certified ('moto g8 power' on the certified-device list).
caveats: Same platform risks as Moto G8: third-party UW exposure on 2020 Motorola HALs historically blocked despite the 118-deg advertised module — runtime probe almost certain to decide this; CONTROL_ZOOM_RATIO requires the Android 11 update. Snapdragon 665 encoder family reliable but thermal sustain (11 nm budget) unproven. ARCore certified (IMU/timestamp likely). Discontinued, Android 11 max.

notes: Brazil/LatAm-only member of the One family (Jul 2020): 48 MP main + 8 MP UW + 5 MP macro + 2 MP depth. Not sold in India. Discontinued. ARCore certified ('motorola one fusion', Depth API).
caveats: ARCore certified with Depth API (good IMU/timestamp signal) and Snapdragon 710 sits in the reliable Qualcomm encoder family, but third-party access to the 118-deg UW on 2020 Motorola HALs is the era GameChanger documented as hidden — UW gate unverifiable without a probe. Thermal sustain on a 10 nm 2018-design SoC unproven. Discontinued, Android 11 max, Brazil-only.

notes: Launched India Jun 2020 at Rs 16,999 (Flipkart) and Brazil Jul 2020 (~R$2.999). 64 MP main + 8 MP UW + 5 MP macro + 2 MP depth, pop-up selfie. Discontinued. ARCore certified ('motorola one fusion+', Depth API).
caveats: Best of the 2020 batch on paper (SD 730G reliable encoder family, ARCore certified with Depth API, sold in both target markets), but the decisive UW gate is unverifiable: 2020 Motorola HALs hid aux camera IDs from third parties and sub-1.0 CONTROL_ZOOM_RATIO support is doubtful on this generation — runtime probe will decide. Thermal sustain unproven. Discontinued, Android 11 max.

notes: Brazil launch Sep 2020 (~R$2.249). 64 MP main + 8 MP UW + 2+2. India only got the G9 (Play) / G9 Power, which lack ultrawides. Discontinued. ARCore certified ('moto g9 plus', Depth API).
caveats: Same profile as One Fusion+ (SD 730G, ARCore certified w/ Depth API): encoder family reliable, IMU/timestamp likely, but third-party UW reachability on 2020 Motorola HALs unverified and historically blocked — probe-decided. Thermal sustain unproven. Discontinued, Android 11 max, Brazil-only.

notes: India launch Nov 30 2020 at Rs 20,999 (Flipkart/motorola.in); Brazil early 2021. 48 MP main + 8 MP UW + 2 MP macro. US sibling = Motorola One 5G Ace. Discontinued. ARCore certified ('moto g 5G', Depth API).
caveats: Snapdragon 750G (8 nm, reliable Qualcomm encoder family) and ARCore certified with Depth API — the IMU/timestamp/encoder side is the strongest of the 2020-21 Motos. Still gated on the unverifiable: third-party Camera2 access to the 118-deg UW on this Motorola generation was historically hidden; needs the runtime zoom-ratio/separate-ID probe. Thermal sustain plausible on 8 nm but unmeasured. Discontinued, Android 11 max.

notes: Europe-first; reached Brazil Oct 22 2020 at R$2.999 (Motorola + Claro stores). Never officially launched in India. 48 MP + 8 MP UW + 5 MP macro + 2 MP depth. Discontinued. ARCore certification: 'moto g 5G plus' absent by name from the certified list, but its hardware-identical US sibling 'motorola one 5G' IS certified (Depth API).
caveats: ARCore certification inferred via the hardware-identical Motorola One 5G (the G 5G Plus name itself is not on the list mirror) — treat IMU/timestamp as likely, not pass. Snapdragon 765 = reliable encoder family. UW gate is the blocker: 118-deg module advertised but 2020 Motorola third-party aux-camera hiding applies; probe-decided. Thermal unproven. Discontinued, Android 11 max, Brazil-only.

notes: Same quad camera (48 MP + 8 MP UW + 2+2). Brazil sold the G10 (Mar 2021, ~R$1.599); India sold the G10 Power (6,000 mAh, Rs 9,999, Mar 2021, Flipkart). Android 12 update was on Motorola's official schedule (by May 2022); rollout varied by region — max version kept at 12 but not independently confirmed per-region. Discontinued. ARCore: 'moto g(10)' is certified; the G10 Power is not separately listed (same capri platform assumed covered).
caveats: Snapdragon 460 is a 4-series — recon intel rates SD 4-series HEVC encode 'mixed, thin data', so the CBR gate is unknown, not likely. Gyroscope present and the G10 is ARCore certified (IMU/timestamp likely), but this is a sub-Rs 10K budget device: UW third-party exposure on Motorola budget HALs almost certainly blocked, and 25-min 1080p30 thermal sustain on an 11 nm entry SoC is doubtful. Android 12 max not independently confirmed per region. Combined row covers two SKUs with different markets (G10 = BR, G10 Power = IN). Expect compat-check rejection in practice.

notes: Brazil launch May 4 2021 at R$1.699 (official Motorola Brazil store). 48 MP + 8 MP UW + 2+2, 90 Hz. Not sold in India. Discontinued. Gyroscope IS present (phonemore/gsmchoice spec sheets). NOT on the ARCore certified-device list. Android 12 max from input — not independently confirmed.
caveats: Highest-risk row in this batch — every gate except GMS is unknown. Unisoc T700 encoder is a data vacuum (recon: zero public CBR/timestamp evidence; recommendation is reject-at-compat-check for Unisoc); NOT ARCore certified, so no IMU-rate or REALTIME-timestamp guarantee (budget Unisoc tier is where UNKNOWN timestamp source and sub-100 Hz HAL caps concentrate); Motorola budget HAL UW hiding applies on top of that. Kept only because nothing is a documented hard fail (gyro present, GMS, 118-deg advertised, Android 11+); in practice expect on-device compat-check rejection. Brazil-only, discontinued.
